newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firm with future, barges active.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firm with future, barges active.

text.p: NWE gas oil firmed on Wednesday after benchmark IPE futures strengthened in the last hour or so of trade.
June IPE gas oil, which expires on Thursday, settled 75 cents higher at $162.25 a tonne, while the July contract settled $1.0 up at $163.75 a tonne.

The barge market was fairly active with a Wall Street trader off-loading some 60-70,000 tonnes of storage material in the afternoon. At least three big players picked up some of the material at about June IPE +50 cents fob AR for balance of the month delivery.

Running refinery was offered at around June IPE +$1.50-$1.75 for balance of June delivery. Sellers justified the high offers with the $1.50 contango between the soon-to-expire June contract and July. Traders said, however, there were no takers at such levels.

Low sulphur diesel barges also traded at higher levels. A small parcel went at the outright price of $169.00 a tonne for balance of June. Another parcel was reported to have traded at June IPE +$7.25 fob ARA.

The cargo side was fairly quiet with premiums for 0.2 percent talked 50 cents below and above July IPE cif NWE and EN590 material pegged at around July IPE +$6.0/+$7.0 cif NWE. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
